statement: Two different integers $u$ and $v$ are written on a board. At each step one of two operations is performed: (i) if $a$ and $b$ are different integers on the board, write $a+b$ if not already there; (ii) if $a$, $b$, $c$ are three different integers on the board and an integer $x$ satisfies $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$, write $x$ if not already there. Determine all pairs $(u, v)$ from which any integer can eventually be written on the board.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $AC > AB$, circumcircle $\Omega$, and incenter $I$. The incircle touches $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ at $D$, $E$, $F$. Let $X$ and $Y$ be points on minor arcs $\widehat{DF}$ and $\widehat{DE}$ of the incircle with $\angle BXD = \angle DYC$. Line $XY$ meets $BC$ at $K$. Let $T$ be the point on $\Omega$ such that $KT$ is tangent to $\Omega$ and $T$ is on the same side of $BC$ as $A$. Prove that $TD$ and $AI$ meet on $\Omega$.

A positive integer $n$ is \textit{peculiar} if for every positive divisor $d$ of $n$, the integer $d(d+1)$ divides $n(n+1)$. Prove that for any four different peculiar positive integers $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $\gcd(A, B, C, D) = 1$.

For a sequence $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_n$ of integers, a pair $(a_i, a_j)$ with $1 \leq i < j \leq n$ is called \textit{interesting} if there exists a pair $(a_k, a_l)$ with $1 \leq k < l \leq n$ such that $\dfrac{a_l - a_k}{a_j - a_i} = 2$. For each $n \geq 3$, find the largest possible number of interesting pairs in a sequence of length $n$.

Find all functions $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every pair of positive integers $(x, y)$: (i) $x$ and $f(x)$ have the same number of positive divisors; (ii) if $x \nmid y$ and $y \nmid x$, then $\gcd(f(x), f(y)) > f(\gcd(x, y))$.
Find all positive integers $d$ for which there exists a degree-$d$ polynomial $P$ with real coefficients such that there are at most $d$ different values among $P(0), P(1), P(2), \ldots, P(d^2 - d)$.
